title: Great GASPI Data Schema
perspective: Samoan Customary Land / Fa’amatai Advocates / Communal Land Defenders

control_zones.governing_authority: Fa’amatai system / communal land holders / extended families (aiga)
control_zones.access_restrictions: Ownership of communal land is vested in the matai title-holding family group; customary land cannot be alienated by sale to non-Samoans or non-members of the title-holding family group, subject to specific exceptions under local law and federal interpretation
strategic_features_located_here: Village territories and settlements across Tutuila, Aunu'u, Ofu, Olosega, and Ta'ū
Cultural and sacred sites (including elevated features of cultural significance)

control_zones.access_restrictions: Subject to standard property laws; less common than customary land; may be alienated or sold under specific conditions
strategic_features_located_here: Some urban areas, including parts of Pago Pago

demographics.notes: Native ethnic Samoans make up the overwhelming majority of the population. The matai (chiefs) hold authority over communal lands on behalf of the aiga (extended families). Demographic data on the proportion of land controlled by aiga is not available in the search results.

named_high_ground_features.name: Mount Matafao
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Highest point on Tutuila Island; control of observation and movement corridors across the central and eastern portions of the main island; position relative to traditional village territories and water resources

named_high_ground_features.name: Mount Pioa (Rainmaker Mountain)
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: High ground near Pago Pago Harbor; control of observation over the harbor and approaches; culturally significant feature linked to matai titles and traditional lands

physical_barriers.name: Federal and Territorial Projects Affecting Communal Land Access
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Various projects and infrastructure developments have affected communal land access over time
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Official justifications often cite public benefit, infrastructure development, or administrative necessity
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Customary land defenders characterize these projects as encroachments on communal lands and disruptions to traditional use and access

agriculture.notes: Communal land includes agricultural and agroforestry areas under customary management. Food import dependency is likely high, as is the case with many Pacific island territories

environmental_degradation_incidents.incident_type: Coastal Erosion and Coral Reef Damage

jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.enforced_system_name: Territorial legal regime under U.S. federal authority / American Samoa Constitution
jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.preferred_or_prior_system_name: Fa’amatai system and Samoan customary law / Deed of Cession protections
enforced_statutes_cited: Local statutes restricting the sale of communal land to non-Samoans (e.g., 21 ASC Chapter 75, or similar provisions)

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: U.S. constitutional norms (Equal Protection, due process) and free-alienation market principles
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Customary prohibition on permanent alienation of communal land / communal land tenure under Samoan custom
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Tension between U.S. constitutional and market principles which generally favor free alienation of property, and the Samoan customary system (fa’amatai) which is based on communal land tenure and prohibits permanent alienation of customary land to non-Samoans or non-members of the title-holding family group. Local statutes are designed to restrict the sale of communal land to non-Samoans, supported by the Deed of Cession protections.

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: Territorial legal regime of the United States
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Samoan political status and fa’amatai governance
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Tension between U.S. constitutional birthright citizenship norms and the continued non-citizen national status of persons born in American Samoa. This unique status affects the political and legal position of Samoans within the U.S. framework.

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Local statutes designed to restrict the sale of communal land to non-Samoans are supported as a means of protecting the Samoan cultural system and communal land tenure, drawing on the Deed of Cession protections.
The U.S. federal government maintains the distinct immigration and nationality status of American Samoa
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Local and customary advocates, including the fa’amatai system, view this status as a limitation on the political and legal rights of Samoans
